node.title: The Minimal Information a Transformation Needs
node.reading:
Every transformation of a technology estate — rationalization, automation and AI enablement, process mining, guardrails, or data modernization — depends on a minimum set of information about what is being changed. The exact information required varies by transformation, but it normally includes a subset of the following: the boundary of the object or process, its accountable owner, its authoritative data sources, and the costs, dependencies, usage, value, or risks relevant to the intervention.

In practice, this information is often missing and rarely treated as a cost and risk of the project itself. It is assumed to be already available or to be supplied by the organization, so producing it does not enter the business case. When it cannot be provided, the project is described as blocked by organizational unreadiness rather than by an unpriced requirement of the method.

This paper argues that estimating the cost and risk of producing this minimum information can improve the business case and help organizations avoid transformations whose full cost may exceed their expected value. It also proposes that this measure may help predict transformation success or failure, a proposition that can be tested against past projects. A companion paper examines how this unpriced cost accumulates and is ultimately paid in human intelligence.

relations: The calibration example makes the minimum-information problem concrete: an application inventory alone may not reveal what would be lost.
El caso no cuantifica un umbral mínimo universal. Una revisión acotada puede omitir dependencias no conocidas, que deben permanecer explícitas.
The minimum information for an architecture decision may include an operator's situated judgment, making its acquisition a real project cost.
El mínimo depende de la decisión, y la observación puede alterar la práctica que intenta describir.
A transformation business case should include the costs of looking, making binding declarations and absorbing their consequences, not only implementation expenditure.
No son tarifas ni porcentajes universales. Un esfuerzo de preparación real no es por sí mismo compensación evitable.
The capture-to-architecture step helps target the minimum information needed for a decision rather than treating complete documentation as the prerequisite for all action.
No se elimina la investigación ni se afirma que cualquier muestreo pequeño baste para toda la empresa.
Upstream work should produce a focusable mission and explicit residual uncertainty before execution is compressed, with the cost of that preparation visible.
Suficiente depende del alcance y del riesgo; no se propone un umbral universal ni una fase de diagnóstico sin límite.
The GEPLAN field account illustrates how incident investigation exposed the operational information that implementation initially lacked.
La lectura retrospectiva no demuestra que el protocolo Cost of Clarity se utilizara entonces ni cuantifica su coste.
The minimum-information lens turns an attractive target into an actionable transition question: what must be known, decided and authorized for the next move to become possible?
La ficha propuesta no asegura una solución Pareto-mejor ni sustituye negociación, financiación o requisitos regulatorios.
Task-sufficient compression suggests asking which distinctions change the transformation decision, rather than treating more contextual data as sufficient by default.
La utilidad formal depende de modelo y fuentes cualificados; no constituye un ahorro medido en una organización.
